# We act for Fernhill Robotics, Inc., the licensee. Quillon Technologies, Inc. has circulated its first draft of the Patent and Software License Agreement with S…

## What field of use does the draft license grant?

The Field is narrowed from 'agricultural and warehouse robotics' to 'autonomous agricultural harvesting robots', dropping warehouse robotics entirely. [F1]

## Is the license grant exclusive, and in what territory?

Section 2.1 grants only a non-exclusive license, contrary to the term sheet's exclusive license in the Field in North America. [F2]

## What royalty rate does the draft license set?

The draft royalty is 5.5%, not the agreed 3.5%. [F3]

## On what base are royalties calculated under the draft?

The royalty base is Gross Sales of the entire Licensed Product (the whole robot) instead of Net Sales of the GraspCore gripper module only. [F4]

## How long are royalties payable, and do they continue after the licensed patents expire?

Section 4.2 requires royalties whether or not any Licensed Patent remains in force, in a perpetual agreement — post-expiration patent royalties are unenforceable under Brulotte v. Thys [EXTERNAL AUTHORITY — NOT IN RECORD; VERIFY BEFORE RELIANCE] and Kimble v. Marvel [EXTERNAL AUTHORITY — NOT IN RECORD; VERIFY BEFORE RELIANCE], and the term sheet ends royalties on expiry of the last Valid Claim. [F5]

## What is the status of patent P-3?

P-3 (US-SYN-0003) lapsed on 2025-03-10 for non-payment of the 7.5-year maintenance fee and should be removed or carry no royalty. [F6] [F14]

## Who is the recorded owner of patent P-4?

P-4's recorded owner is Quillon Labs GmbH and the assignment to Quillon Technologies is not recorded, so Licensor may not be able to license it; require a recorded assignment or joinder of Quillon Labs. [F7]

## What is the status of P-5?

P-5 (US-SYN-0005) is a pending application, not a granted patent; it should not support royalties until it issues. [F8]

## Who owns improvements under the draft license?

Section 6.1 assigns all Licensee improvements to Licensor, whereas the term sheet gives Licensor only a non-exclusive, royalty-free grant-back license. [F9]

## What termination rights does the Licensor have under the draft?

Section 10.2 lets Licensor terminate if Fernhill challenges the validity of any Licensed Patent — a no-challenge clause not in the term sheet and in tension with Lear v. Adkins [EXTERNAL AUTHORITY — NOT IN RECORD; VERIFY BEFORE RELIANCE]; delete it. [F10]

## What warranties and indemnities does the Licensor give against infringement?

Section 8.3 disclaims non-infringement and any duty to defend or indemnify, contrary to the agreed IP indemnity capped at royalties paid in the prior 24 months. [F11]

## Can the Licensee assign the agreement, for example on a sale of its business?

Section 14.1 bars Fernhill from assigning, even on a change of control, without Licensor's consent in its sole discretion; the term sheet allows assignment to a successor in a sale of the business. [F12]

## Is there a minimum annual royalty, and from when?

The minimum annual royalty is $250,000 from the first license year instead of the agreed $150,000 starting in the second year. [F13]

## Does the licensed GraspCore software include open-source components, and under what licenses?

Schedule B shows motion-planner-core under GPL-3.0-only, statically linked into GraspCore — a copyleft obligation that contradicts Licensor's s.8.2 warranty and makes s.2.2's object-code-only distribution restriction impossible to comply with. [F14]

## Does the draft provide for source-code escrow?

The draft omits the agreed source-code escrow (release on insolvency or discontinued support); add an escrow clause. [F15]

## Authorities Requiring Verification

The following 3 legal authorities cited above do not appear in the matter record and were NOT verified by BigLaw. Confirm each against a citator before any reliance:

- Brulotte v. Thys
- Kimble v. Marvel
- Lear v. Adkins
